metadata.title: Identity Core

links.text: BRM BC220 – Identity and Access Management

metadata.remarks:
Identity Core defines the foundational institutional identity capability. Identity is established as a persistent trust object, authoritative independently of authentication mechanisms, authorization decisions, federation relationships, or lifecycle automation.

Governance and Responsibility Anchor:
This pattern is the authoritative anchor for roles and responsibilities, SSPPs, standards, procedures, guidelines, and assurance activities within scope. Controls are intentionally applied at the pattern level. Sub-capabilities are descriptive only and do not carry independent control or assurance scope.

components.title: Identity Authority
components.description: Defines the authoritative institutional source(s) of truth for identity existence and core attributes.

components.title: Identity Namespace
components.description: Defines the namespace(s) and identifier schemes used to avoid ambiguity in identity representation.

components.title: Identity Uniqueness
components.description: Ensures each identity corresponds to a single subject and prevents collision or duplication.

components.title: Identity Attribution
components.description: Ensures actions can be reliably attributed to a specific identity for accountability and audit.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Authoritative digital identities must be defined and governed. (NIST 800-171r3 IA-1)
Unique identity assignment must be enforced. (NIST 800-171r3 IA-2)
Identity attributes must maintain integrity across the lifecycle. (NIST 800-171r3 IA-5)
Access control policy must rely on authoritative identities. (NIST 800-171r3 AC-1)
Enhanced identity governance applies to high-risk and privileged identities. (NIST 800-172r3 IA-7)
Identity architecture must be formally defined and governed. (NIST 800-172r3 PL-8)
